flagged.evidence: The item defines “φ:C_0(I;Z)→Z” as a cochain, but then says “no finite singular 0-chain can equal it.” A finite chain is an element of C_0(I;Z), whereas φ is an element of Hom(C_0(I;Z),Z). No identification or representation map between these distinct types is defined, so the refuted claim and asserted conclusion are not well-formed.

[L5] says homotopy-equivalent spaces have isomorphic fundamental groups “because induced maps on π_1 are functorial and invariant under based homotopy,” citing thm-induced-fundamental-group-map-functoriality. That dependency applies only to pointed maps f:(X,x_0)→(Y,y_0) and homotopies that keep x_0 at y_0. A homotopy equivalence supplies ordinary, not based, homotopies; a change-of-basepoint argument is required and is neither stated nor cited.

[L2] attributes the condition “g_n-f_n=d^D_{n+1}s_n+s_{n-1}d^C_n” to def-chain-homotopy. The cited definition instead requires, for s:f≃g, “f_n-g_n=d^D_{n+1}s_n+s_{n-1}d^C_n.” Thus the prism identity g_#-f_#=∂P_H+P_H∂ makes P_H a homotopy in the opposite displayed direction; the proof would need −P_H for the asserted direction.

The definition gives only an integral product C_p(X;Z)×C_q(Y;Z)→C_{p+q}(X×Y;Z), then says “and then tensor with coefficients when needed.” It does not specify coefficient groups, a coefficient pairing, or a target. For arbitrary abelian groups the canonical construction has target with tensor-product coefficients (for example G⊗H), not an unspecified copy of G.

Step 1.2 says “The face opposite the vertex (v_i,1) is the bottom face of λ_i, and the face opposite (v_i,0) is the top face.” For n=1 and i=0, λ_0 has vertices (v_0,0),(v_0,1),(v_1,1); the face opposite (v_0,1) is the diagonal from (v_0,0) to (v_1,1), not the bottom edge. The claimed face classification used in the boundary argument is false.

The statement takes a∈C_p(X;G) and b∈C_q(Y;G) and writes (f×g)_#(a×b), but the cited cross-product definition supplies no coefficient-level operation or target. With arbitrary coefficient groups, the standard product would land in C_{p+q}(X×Y;G⊗G), and the left induced map must consequently have G⊗G coefficients. Neither that target nor a map G⊗G→G is specified.
